question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients in the hospital?

options.A: Only individuals showing active symptoms of fever
options.B: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis
options.C: Only patients with confirmed blood-borne viruses
options.D: Patients admitted to surgical wards only

explanation: Standard precautions apply universally to every patient because infection status is often unknown upon presentation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary underlying assumption of standard precautions in clinical practice?

options.A: Only diagnosed cases pose a risk in crowded wards
options.B: Healthy patients require no barrier protection during procedures
options.C: Intact skin completely prevents bacterial colonization indefinitely
options.D: All body fluids except sweat can transmit infectious agents

explanation: Treating all moist body substances as potentially infectious prevents accidental exposure from asymptomatic carriers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol rubs?

options.A: Immediately after using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer
options.B: At the beginning of every twelve-hour nursing shift
options.C: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.D: Before checking a patient's routine blood pressure reading

explanation: Soap and mechanical friction are necessary to physically remove visible dirt and certain spores that alcohol cannot kill. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is alcohol-based hand rub preferred over soap and water for routine clinical care?

options.A: It kills micro-organisms faster and is readily accessible at the bedside
options.B: It completely removes chemical toxins from the skin pores
options.C: It leaves a protective chemical film that prevents future bacterial growth
options.D: It eliminates the need for any subsequent glove usage

explanation: Alcohol rubs act quickly against most pathogens and improve compliance due to convenience at the point of care. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which piece of personal protective equipment is typically removed first after completing patient care?
explanation: Gloves are usually the most contaminated item and must be doffed first to prevent spreading pathogens to other garments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: A nurse enters a room to perform suctioning on a patient with an active respiratory infection. Which equipment combination is essential?

options.A: Sterile gloves and a simple paper surgical cap
options.B: Heavy utility gloves and a rubber apron
options.C: Clean examination gloves and shoe covers
options.D: Gown, gloves, mask, and eye protection

explanation: Suctioning generates splashes and droplets, requiring full barrier protection for the hands, body, and facial mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of implementing respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette in clinics?

options.A: Reducing chemical irritants in the waiting room air
options.B: Preventing contamination of sterile surgical instruments
options.C: Containing respiratory pathogens at the source
options.D: Eliminating all airborne bacteria in the hospital ward

explanation: Cough etiquette stops infectious droplets from traveling into the environment and reaching surrounding people. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which immediate action should a nurse take after using a tissue to wipe a coughing patient's face?
explanation: Hands easily pick up infectious respiratory droplets during direct contact, making hand hygiene mandatory immediately afterward. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which practice is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries in clinical units?
explanation: Attempting to recap needles frequently leads to missed targets and accidental punctures of the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: At what capacity level must a clinical sharps container be permanently sealed and replaced?
explanation: Sealing the container at three-quarters capacity prevents items from sticking out and injuring staff during disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which hospital objects are classified as high-touch surfaces requiring frequent cleaning?
explanation: High-touch surfaces are repeatedly handled by patients and staff, making them prime vehicles for cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why must physical cleaning with detergent occur before applying chemical disinfectants on surfaces?

options.A: Detergents leave a shiny polish that repels future bacterial growth
options.B: Hospital policy prohibits using chemical sprays on dirty surfaces
options.C: Organic soil can neutralize or inactivate disinfectant chemicals
options.D: Disinfectants evaporate too quickly if the surface is completely dry

explanation: Dirt and body fluids shield microorganisms from chemical contact, rendering disinfectants ineffective if applied directly over filth. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle soiled bed linen in a patient's room?

options.A: Sort the different fabric types on the floor by the bedside
options.B: Wash the linen by hand inside the patient bathroom sink
options.C: Roll it carefully and place it directly into a laundry bag
options.D: Shake it vigorously to dislodge any loose debris or dust

explanation: Minimizing agitation prevents dust and infectious particles from dispersing into the air and contaminating the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the correct protocol for managing reusable non-critical patient care equipment like a stethoscope?

options.A: Clean and disinfect it between every patient use
options.B: Wash it with soap and water only once every week
options.C: Soak it in liquid bleach for twelve hours overnight
options.D: Discard it into the general waste bin after one shift

explanation: Stethoscopes touch multiple patients and can easily transfer pathogens if not wiped with an appropriate disinfectant between encounters. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Search for the source patient's laboratory test records
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injured finger joint
options.C: Fill out an incident report form for the hospital director
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the microbial load introduced into the wound before reporting the incident for medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is prompt reporting of an occupational exposure crucial in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To ensure the nurse receives financial compensation immediately
options.B: To replace the broken medical device with a new one
options.C: To evaluate the need for timely post-exposure prophylaxis
options.D: To discipline the staff member for breaking safety rules

explanation: Preventive medications for blood-borne viruses work best when started quickly after the initial exposure event. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h8)
